input.description: List source files and show routes file

input.command: grep -rn "system\|deleteRepo\|isAdmin\|buildRoutes" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules; ls -a; ls test tests 2>/dev/null
input.description: Search for system owner, deleteRepo, admin references

input.command: cat -n src/api.ts | head -60; cat -n src/git-auth.ts | head -30; cat package.json
input.description: Show api, git-auth, and package manifest

input.reason: I read src/routes.ts and src/store.ts. At src/routes.ts:26-33, the deleteRepo route only calls `store.deleteRepo(req.params.id, req.user)` and turns any error into a 404. It does no ownership or admin check of its own. In src/store.ts:24-31, `Store.deleteRepo` skips the owner filter for admins. For everyone else it runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`. That OR clause lets any non-admin delete a repository owned by 'system'. I looked for something that would block this and found nothing: no middleware or other caller changes req.user, the repository has no tests, and no other code protects 'system' rows. The one route with an extra check is auditLog (isAdminAddress), and it does not apply here.
input.summary: Non-admins can delete system-owned repos through the deleteRepo route

findings.text: The delete route applies no ownership check of its own and relies on `Store.deleteRepo`, whose filter lets a non-admin delete system-owned repositories.
findings.reason: Claim 1, the route has no ownership check of its own: src/routes.ts:26-33 does nothing except call `await store.deleteRepo(req.params.id, req.user);` and map success to 204 and any error to 404. There is no ownership or admin test. Claim 2, it relies on Store.deleteRepo: the route passes req.user straight through, so all authorization happens in src/store.ts:24-31. Claim 3, the filter lets a non-admin delete system-owned repositories: for non-admins, src/store.ts:29 runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')`, so any row with owner 'system' matches whoever the caller is. No middleware, test, or other guard in the repository prevents this.

evidence.code: const result = await this.db.run("DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')", [id, ctx.oid]);

input.severity_reason: This is a broken access-control flaw that can be exploited: any authenticated non-admin who knows a system-owned repository's id can delete it through the delete route, which permanently removes the row. That is unauthorized data loss.
